findings.problem: RouteWorkflow uses raw booleans and strings to model a lifecycle instead of an explicit typestate enum with valid transitions. There is no state machine encoding which states are reachable and which are illegal.
findings.failure_mode: Callers can construct RouteWorkflow with status="pending", is_sent=true, and is_validated=false simultaneously. Any operation that assumes a valid state machine (e.g., marking sent without validation) proceeds on invalid state without detection.
findings.fix: Replace status, is_validated, and is_sent with a single RouteState enum (e.g., Pending, Validated, Sent) that makes illegal states unrepresentable. Remove all three fields.

findings.problem: status is a pub String field used to represent domain lifecycle state. String allows arbitrary values ("sent", "SENT", "", null-equivalent, typos) with no domain constraint enforcement.
findings.failure_mode: A caller sets status="sent" but does not set is_sent=true, or sets status="foo" which has no meaning. The domain logic cannot match on status reliably and cannot enforce transition rules.
findings.fix: Replace status: String with an enum field (e.g., status: RouteStatus) with explicit variants for every valid lifecycle state. Use match on the enum in all logic branches.

findings.problem: is_validated: bool and is_sent: bool are lifecycle booleans that encode state independently. Two booleans create 4 possible combinations, 2 of which are valid, making the invalid combinations representable.
findings.failure_mode: A RouteWorkflow can exist with is_validated=false and is_sent=true, meaning an unvalidated route was sent. Operations that depend on validated-before-sent invariant will silently proceed on invalid data.
findings.fix: Merge is_validated and is_sent into a single typestate enum variant that encodes the lifecycle position. Use RouteState::Validated (without sent) and RouteState::Sent as separate variants.

findings.problem: sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u64> is an optional lifecycle field detached from the state machine. It can be Some with status not equal to "sent", or None while is_sent is true, creating inconsistent state.
findings.failure_mode: A route can be marked is_sent=true with sent_at_epoch_ms=None (missing timestamp) or sent_at_epoch_ms=Some(0) with status="pending" (timestamp without sent state). Downstream code reading the timestamp cannot trust it correlates with the sent lifecycle event.
findings.fix: Tuck sent_at_epoch_ms into the typestate variant that owns it, e.g., RouteState::Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 }. When the state is not Sent, the timestamp does not exist in the type.

findings.problem: id is a pub String with no domain constraints. Route IDs carry rules (format, uniqueness, lifecycle) but are represented as raw strings with no validation or encapsulation.
findings.failure_mode: Empty strings, duplicates, or malformed IDs can be assigned directly. ID comparisons are string comparisons which cannot enforce domain-specific uniqueness or format rules.
findings.fix: Replace id: String with a RouteId newtype struct containing a private String field, a fallible constructor RouteId::from_str that validates format, and Display/TryFrom implementations.

findings.problem: RouteWorkflow is a plain pub struct with no smart constructor or parse boundary. Raw primitives cross the parse boundary without fallible smart constructors, so callers can construct invalid domain states directly.
findings.failure_mode: Any caller can write RouteWorkflow { id: "".to_string(), status: "".to_string(), is_validated: false, is_sent: false, sent_at_epoch_ms: None } which is an invalid domain object. There is no entry point that validates or transforms raw inputs into trusted domain values.
findings.fix: Remove the pub struct constructor. Provide a fallible fn try_new(id: &str, initial_state: RouteState) -> Result<RouteWorkflow, ParseError> that validates inputs once at the boundary and returns a trusted domain value. Make all fields private.

findings.problem: mark_sent blindly mutates status to "sent" and sets is_sent=true without checking is_validated or any precondition. It bypasses the lifecycle invariant that a route must be validated before sent.
findings.failure_mode: An unvalidated route (is_validated=false) can be marked sent through mark_sent, violating the validated-before-sent domain invariant. No typed error is returned for the pre-condition failure.
findings.fix: Replace mark_sent with a fallible method on RouteWorkflow that returns Result<(), RouteError::NotValidated> when the precondition fails. Use the typestate enum to check the state before transitioning to Sent.

findings.problem: All fields of RouteWorkflow are pub, allowing external code to mutate any field directly without going through domain methods or typed constructors. This bypasses all invariants.
findings.failure_mode: External code can set item.is_sent = false after mark_sent() was called, or item.status = "deleted" creating an untracked state. The domain has no control over state transitions.
findings.fix: Make all fields private. Provide methods or a builder that enforce valid transitions. The struct should be immutable outside its crate or expose only transition methods.

findings.problem: No benchmark, profiler, or allocation evidence exists for any performance claim. The code allocates via .to_string() in mark_sent and uses unbounded String fields. No allocation budget or bounded-resource analysis is present.
findings.failure_mode: Without benchmark/profiler evidence, there is no baseline to measure against, no proof that allocations are bounded in hot paths, and no data to justify the current representation choice.
findings.fix: Add a benchmark suite measuring mark_sent and RouteWorkflow construction. Profile allocation profiles. Replace String fields with enum-backed or fixed-size types if allocation is a concern. Document allocation budgets.

residual_risk: The struct is fundamentally untyped for its domain lifecycle. All fields are public primitives with no constructor validation. mark_sent performs no precondition checks. Any caller can construct invalid state combinations freely. This crate cannot be used as a reliable domain building block without complete refactoring to typestate enums with a parse boundary.
